speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To help me understand your condition better, could you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms and if they radiate from your neck down to your arm?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (or severe Cervical Radiculopathy with C8/T1 involvement).

*Note: Based on the patient's history of burning pain, paresthesias in the hands, progressive bilateral hand weakness, and risk factors like diabetes, this clinical picture strongly suggests a compressive cervical myelopathy. A Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the cervical spine is the definitive test required to confirm the diagnosis and assess the extent of spinal cord compression.*
